data.one_liner: Access Android AlarmManager service and run Dart code in the background.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter applications to access the Android AlarmManager service. Enables running custom Dart code in background background isolates when alarms fire, even if the main app has ended.
use_when: You need to trigger recurring tasks or one-off alarms on Android at precise times.
You need background tasks to execute when the app is closed or not in the foreground.
avoid_when: You need cross-platform background task handling that includes iOS.
Your app targets Android 14+ and you cannot handle SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM permissions via additional plugins.
strengths: Integrates directly with native Android AlarmManager service.
Supports periodic and one-shot background alarms with custom callbacks.
weaknesses: Android only (no iOS or web support documented).
Alarms are cleared if the device is rebooted unless properly configured, and will not fire if the app is force-stopped.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding permissions and receiver/service components to AndroidManifest.xml, plus handling SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM permissions for Android 14+ via an additional plugin like permission_handler.
